## LLM Recipe

### 1.2 Model Architecture &amp; Scaling Laws

#### [Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06206>)

A controlled BabyLM study compares repeated shared layers with deeper independent layers and tests whether recurrence mitigates the grammaticality drop associated with multimodal training. Its matched controls show why changing text composition and batching must be separated from the contribution of visual input.

**Published:** 2026-11-04 · **First seen:** 2026-11-09T11:03:40.430+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Recurrent Depth, Multimodal Pretraining, Controlled Experiments

**Public availability:** 2026-11-05T01:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06206v1>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/datasets/daichihotta/babyloop-mm-corpus>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Methods, main results, limitations and reproducibility/seed/no-image controls inspected. At 100M unique words and 1B repeated-word exposure, the 97M-parameter text-only looped model exceeds the 48-layer model by 5.36 BLiMP points at matched inference compute, over three seeds. The primary multimodal interaction is −0.01 points, with pooled 95% interval \[−1.44, 1.41\]. This is a retrospectively reviewed November 5 paper announcement, not a new dataset release.

**Limitations:** Recurrence is confounded with text-input injection; inference compute is not total training-cost matching. One frozen image vector and altered language sources limit generalization. Only the looped model has a batch-matched no-image decomposition, and several exploratory comparisons are unadjusted. The linked corpus predates this study; no author training-code release was verified.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.3 Context Engineering &amp; Memory

#### [Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06500>)

CocaCola compresses a tool observation into task- and reasoning-conditioned latent vectors, training the compressor to preserve a frozen agent’s next-action behavior rather than reconstruct the original text. This can shrink the agent’s context while retaining useful retrieval evidence, provided the deployment supports direct embedding inputs.

**Published:** 2026-11-04 · **First seen:** 2026-11-09T11:06:58.728+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Latent Compression, Tool Observations, White-box Agents

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.06500v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. V1 methods, four-dataset evaluation and training appendices inspected. Across two agent–encoder pairs, the authors report 70.01–89.24% fewer agent input/output tokens and 24.45–55.97% lower measured runtime than uncompressed retrieval, with improved exact match on all four QA datasets. Paper receipt and repository release are November 4; this is retrospective catch-up for November 5, without asserting an exact first-public hour.

**Limitations:** Compression uses an additional encoder GPU and requires white-box embeddings. Pair-level train/validation splitting need not separate questions. Released compressed and baseline harnesses use different backends and limits, so the code does not verify a matched reproduction of headline latency; checkpoints were not verified. No independent reproduction.

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [A thousand fewer paths to root](<https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/>)

OpenAI’s agent pipeline turns candidate kernel bugs into evidence-backed reports through separate discovery, reproduction, impact assessment, patching and human review. The disclosure shows why agent evaluation must verify both an outcome and the path that produced it, and where automated triage can reduce review bottlenecks.

**Published:** 2026-11-04 · **First seen:** 2026-11-09T11:05:44.548+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Security Agents, Runtime Validation, Agent Harnesses

[Blog](<https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The full November 4 disclosure reports 2,308 deduplicated candidates, 1,724 dynamically reproduced vulnerabilities and 948 distinct local-privilege-escalation patch groups from an October campaign costing about $1.21M in API credits. An early 200-success run contained 20 exploits using the wrong vulnerability, motivating an independent assigned-vulnerability check. Retrospective catch-up retains the disclosure date and older experiment timing.

**Limitations:** Author-run results with an unreleased cyber model and withheld implementation details. Some findings were already patched or public before campaign review ended. API credits exclude complete operational costs, and hypothetical bounties are not realized returns. The separate kernelCTF experiment dropped an incompatible mitigation; it is not identical to the public program.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.8 Hardware, Networking &amp; Cluster Efficiency

#### [flash-comm: Self-Synchronizing Collective Communication for LLM Decoding](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06634>)

flash-comm attaches readiness information to transferred data so decoding collectives can proceed without separate steady-state group barriers. Hardware-calibrated protocol selection and consistent reduction ordering lower communication latency while keeping participating GPUs’ results aligned.

**Published:** 2026-11-04 · **First seen:** 2026-11-09T11:06:58.206+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Collective Communication, Decode Latency, NVLink

**Public availability:** 2026-11-05T01:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06634v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Complete 11-page v1, Sections 1–8, Appendix A and all tables inspected. Within one NVLink/NVSwitch domain, hardware/group/message-specific selection switches among sentinel and sequence-packet protocols. Eight-B300 all-reduce tests show a 28.8% median latency reduction versus SGLang custom all-reduce v2; one DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 tensor-parallel-8 decode workload reports 1.7–6.8% lower time per output token at concurrency 16–512. Retrospective November 5 catch-up preserves the November 4 receipt and schedule-inferred first announcement.

**Limitations:** Evaluation covers 2/4/8-GPU H100, H200 and B300 groups, supported aligned BF16/FP32 layouts and one end-to-end model. Multi-node and all-to-all are future work. Participating ranks must share call order, supported progress assumptions and calibrated protocol tables. Agreement within a collective does not imply numerical identity with every backend. No author implementation or independent reproduction was verified.
